scanMethod: axe-core via Playwright (WCAG 2.1 AA) — homepage scan. Scoring: start 100, deduct 15 per critical, 8 per serious, 4 per moderate, 1 per minor violation. Axe-core detects ~40-57% of real WCAG 2.1 AA issues.

sites.notes: Colorado regional group, multiple rooftops. Relatively clean site. Missing document title and meta-viewport are mobile accessibility issues.

Midwest group, multiple states. Critical violations include missing image alt text and unlabeled form controls — both high-frequency ADA lawsuit triggers. Color contrast and unlabeled links compound the exposure.
Indiana group, multiple rooftops. Missing page language declaration (html-has-lang) affects screen reader users — a WCAG 2.1 AA requirement. Document title issue also present.

Wisconsin group, regional chain. Four serious violations — scrollable regions not keyboard-accessible (scrollable-region-focusable) and missing image alt roles directly affect screen reader and keyboard-only users browsing inventory.

Utah group, regional chain. Unlabeled buttons (button-name) are critical — screen readers cannot identify interactive elements. Improper ARIA usage (aria-prohibited-attr) and color contrast failures add to exposure.

New England group. Unlabeled iframes (frame-title) block screen reader users from embedded content like vehicle search tools or financing widgets. Color contrast and unlabeled links are commonly cited in demand letters.

Mid-Atlantic regional group. Critical image-alt failure means screen readers cannot identify vehicle images — one of the most common violations cited in ADA website demand letters against auto dealers.

Missouri regional group. Cleanest homepage in the set — zero axe-core violations detected. Note: axe-core detects ~50% of real WCAG issues; deeper multi-page crawl (inventory, financing forms) recommended before drawing final conclusions.
Nevada regional group. Single serious violation — color contrast. Low overall risk on homepage, but interior pages (financing, service booking) should be checked.

Utah/West regional chain, multiple rooftops. Unlabeled buttons and form select elements (select-name) directly block screen reader users from vehicle search and contact forms — high litigation risk. Two critical violations.
Southeast/Mid-Atlantic regional group. Missing alt text on vehicle images (critical) and color contrast failures are the two violations cited most often in ADA demand letters targeting auto dealers.
